Revised assessment with literature insight: The statement reflects a flexible inflation-targeting approach consistent with the New Keynesian policy-rule framework (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), pairing strong labor markets and solid business investment with below-2% inflation and a commitment to gradualism. Low market-based inflation compensation suggests anchored expectations—important for policy transmission and term-structure dynamics per macro-finance research (Ang and Piazzesi; Rudebusch and Wu; Rudebusch and Svensson). Strong employment and business fixed investment typically reinforce balance sheets and lower external finance premia, buffering adverse net-worth shocks and supporting continued expansion (Investment Spending Affects External Finance Premium; Employment Reduces Adverse Shocks to Net Worth). The Committee’s emphasis on a symmetric 2% goal and “close monitoring” is consistent with cost-channel considerations, where rate hikes can temporarily lift firms’ marginal costs and inflation pressures (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005; Ravenna and Walsh, 2006). Operationally, maintaining an accommodative stance while using forward guidance and interest on reserves (Goodfriend, 2002) aligns with a gradual path toward normalization.

Overall tone: moderately positive with balanced risks and credible inflation control.
